Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 2024 - 1988 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FERROSILICOCHROMIUM 

( Third Revision ) 



( Reaffirmed 1999) 



1. Scope — This standard covers the requirements and condition of delivery for ferrosilicochromium 
commonly used in iron and steel Industry. 

2. Terminology — For the purpose of this standard the following definitions shall apply. 

2.1 Cast ( Meit ) — The product of any of the following: 

a) One furnace heat, or 

b) One tap of continuous furnace, or 

c) A number of furnace or crucible heats of similar composition mixed in a ladle or holding 
furnace and used for making a cast. 

2.2 Bate!) — A group of ferroalloy lump of one grade cast from the same cast/melt as given in 2.1. 

3. Definition — A master alloy of iron, chromium and silicon with chromium content in the range 
from 28 to 65 percent by mass and silicon content in the range from 10 to 55 percent by mass, obtained 
by reduction from the corresponding raw materials or their concentrates. 

4. Grades — This standard covers four grades of ferrosilicochromium as specified in Table 1.

5. Particulars to be Specified Wliile Ordering ~ For the benefit of the purchaser, particulars to be 
specified while ordering for the material to this specification shall be as follows: 

a) Quantity of the material; 

b) Name of the material; 

c) Grade; 

d) Size range; and 

e) Necessary requirements for analysis reports, packing, etc, as appropriate. 

6. Supply of Materials — General requirements relating to supply of material to this specification 
shall be as laid down in IS : 1387-1967 'General requirements for the supply of metallurgical materials 
{revised)'. 

7. Chemical Composition — Each batch of material shall conform to requirements of chemical 
composition specified in Table 1 and if so specified by the purchaser at the time of enquiry and order, 
shall supply a test certificate of chemical analysis of the sample of material for each melt.

7.1 If specified by the purchaser at the time of enquiry and order that each lump of the batch should 
conform to the chemical composition specified in Table 1, this shall be agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer. 

7.2 The chemical composition given in Table 1 shows only the main constituent elements and usual 
impurities. !f the purchaser requires closer ranges for the main element contents and/or different 
limits for specified elements and/or non-spBcified elements, this shall be agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer. 

7.3 The chemical composition of the material shall be determined either by the method specified in 
IS : 2020 (Part 1 )-1 968 'Analysis of silicon and chromium', or any other established instrumental/ 
chemical method, in case of dispute, the procedure ^iven in the latest verson of IS : 2020 ( Part 1 )- 
1968 shall be the referee method. However, where the method is not given in IS : 2020. referee 
method shall be agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 

7.4 The percentage of residual elements ^iven in Table 2 for various grades of ferrosilicochromium 
shall be maximum. If required by the purchaser, the manufacturer shall furnish an analysis for any of 
these elements on a cumulative basis over a period mutually agreed upon between the purchaser ^nd 
the manufacturer.

8. Size Range —The material is supplied in lumps or as crushed and screened particles. The 
particle size ranges and tolerances shall be as given in Table 3. The undersize values shall be vaiid 
at the point of delivery to purchaser. If neither the producer/seller nor the buyer is responsible for 
transportation, then the point at which the values become valid shall be agreed upon. 

8.1 The particle size specified in Table 3 refers to screening on a steel wire test sieve conforming to 
IS : 460 ( Part 1 )-1985 'Specification for wire cloth test sieves ( third revision Y.

9, Extraneous Contamination — The material shall be reasonably free from extraneous contamina- 
tions like slag and non-metallic inclusions, etc. 

10, Sampling — Each batch of the material shall be sampled in accordance with IS: 1472-197? 
'Methods of sampling ferroalloys for determination of chemical composition ( first revision )'. 

11. Packing— The material shall be supplied packed in a suitable container in quantities mutually 
agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser. 

12. Marking — The material shall be marked with the following: 

a) Supplier's name or trade-mark; 

b) Grade designation and size; 

c) Quantity; 

2 



IS : 2024 - 1988 



d) Date of manufacture; and 

e) Shelf life, if needed. 

12.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1962 and subsequently revised in 1970 and 1979- In view 
of the experience gained during these years, it was felt necessary to revise this standard, [n this 
revision, the following are the main modifications: 

a) Definition of ferrosilicochromium has been Included; 

b) Clauses pertaining to chemical analysis and size range have been modified and aligned with 
latest Indian Standards on ferroalloys; 

c) New clauses have been incorporated to avoid wide segregation of chemical constituents, 
thereby safeguarding the small consumers of this product; and 

d) Grade FeSi40Cr35 has been included.
